# Sub-claims inherit the intent the template declared

A fan-out's sub-claims carry the `intent` the parent claim declared, not a fixed
producer default. Declare a claim read-only and every sub-claim opened under it
is read-only.

## The template

```yaml
name: fanout-intent-r
version: "1"
nodes:
  - type: fan_parent
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    claim_producers:
      - name: claim-producer-filesystem
        selector: data
        intent: r
        alias: data
    error_types:
      "acquire/unavailable": {action: give_up}
    fan_out:
      claim: data
      partition_request: '{"list":[{"key":"s1"},{"key":"s2"},{"key":"s3"}]}'
      error_policy:
        kind: best_effort
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          pk:
            type: string
            source: "{{child.partition_key}}"
```

Change `intent: r` to `intent: rw` for the second run. Nothing else differs.

## Read the handles back

```bash
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/observability/claim-handles?instance_id=$IID&limit=50"
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/events?instance_id=$IID"
```

## What the product does

Under `intent: r` the run opens one parent handle with intent `r` and three
sub-handles. Every sub-handle points at that parent, and every one carries
intent `r`. All four acquisitions the event log records name intent `r` and no
other value.

Under `intent: rw` the same shape produces one parent and three sub-handles all
carrying `rw`.

What the sub-claims carry tracks what the template declared — the part a
template author cannot check by reading the template.
